sources.says: The midrash answers: throw it a scrap and it shuts its mouth, and so were Israel's judges.

56:11.headline: Here נפש means appetite, not soul
56:11.body: נפש is often translated 'soul'. Ibn Ezra says that in the Bible it most often means the drive to eat, so these dogs 'strong of נפש' are dogs with huge appetites.

sources.quote: רוב הנפש הנמצא במקרא על הכח המתאוה לאכל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says נפש in the Bible mostly means the appetite for food.

sources.quote: נפש. ענין תאוה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means desire.

57:1.headline: The righteous man is lost, but only to the people he leaves
57:1.body: אבד usually means lost or destroyed. Radak says the righteous man is not lost to himself, since his soul lives on, but his generation has lost him.

sources.quote: לא ר"ל שהצדיק אבד במותו כי לעצמו לא אבד
sources.says: Radak says the verse does not mean the righteous man himself is lost when he dies.

sources.quote: אלא אבד מדורו כי להם היא האבידה
sources.says: Radak says he is lost from his generation, and the loss is theirs.

57:2.headline: Who walks straight ahead: the righteous man, or peace itself?
57:2.body: נכחו means straight ahead or upright. Rashi and Ibn Ezra say it is the righteous man who walked an upright path. Radak says it is peace that comes straight toward him when he dies.

sources.quote: זֶה שֶׁהָיָה הֹלֵךְ נְכֹחוֹ בְּיָשְׁרוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the one who walked straight, in his uprightness.

sources.quote: השלום שזכר יבא נכח הצדיק בהאספו
sources.says: Radak says the peace the verse mentions comes toward the righteous man as he dies.

57:5.headline: A rock's “branches”: a tree word borrowed for cliffs
57:5.body: סעיף is a branch of a tree. Here it names the jagged ledges of a cliff, which stick out from the rock the way a branch sticks out from a tree.

sources.quote: והוא מושאל מענף היוצא מן האילן אשר יקרא סעיף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word is borrowed from a branch growing out of a tree.

sources.quote: נקרא כן לפי שהוא לסלע כמו הסעיף לאילן
sources.says: Radak says it is called this because it is to the rock what a branch is to a tree.

57:6.headline: Smooth stones become your portion: חלקי and חלקך
57:6.body: חלקי נחל are the smooth stones of a stream, which people worshipped. The next word, חלקך, means your portion. Radak says the prophet chose the two look-alike words on purpose.

sources.quote: ואמר חלקי ואמר חלקך לשון נופל על הלשון
sources.says: Radak says saying חלקי and then חלקך is a play of one word on another.

sources.quote: כשהיו מוצאין אבן חלקה ויפה באבני הנחל היו עובדים לה
sources.says: Radak says when they found a smooth, pretty stone in the stream, they worshipped it.

57:8.headline: Behind the doorpost: a reminder of idols, or incense?
57:8.body: זכרון usually means a reminder. Radak says they put a reminder of their idols behind the door, the reverse of the mezuzah God gave them. He also cites a reading where it means incense, like the offering called אזכרה.

sources.quote: אני נתתי לך מצות מזוזה שתזכרי תמיד עבודתי
sources.says: Radak has God say he gave them the mezuzah so they would always remember him.

sources.quote: כלומר שמת קטרת לעכו"ם אחר הדלת והמזוזה
sources.says: Radak cites a reading that they put incense for idols behind the door and doorpost.

sources.quote: כמו וזכרו כיין לבנון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra compares it to the fragrance called זכר in Hosea, and to the אזכרה offering.

57:9.headline: Did she bring gifts, go to see, or travel to the king?
57:9.body: Saadia and Metzudat Zion tie ותשורי to תשורה, a gift. Rashi and Ibn Ezra tie it to אשורנו, to see, and Radak reads it as to travel.

sources.quote: ותשורי פירש רב סעדיה ז"ל מענין תשורה שהוא מנחה
sources.says: Radak reports that Saadia reads it as תשורה, a gift.

sources.quote: ואני פירשתיו בספר השרשים כמו ותלכי
sources.says: Radak says that in his book of roots he read it as and you went.

sources.quote: והנה ותשורי כמו אשורנו, הלכת לראות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like אשורנו, I see him: you went to see.

57:10.headline: The “life of your hand”: Rashi reads it through Arabic
57:10.body: חית ידך literally reads “the life of your hand.” Rashi says חית is an Arabic word for need, so you found what you needed. Radak and Ibn Ezra read it as strength.

sources.quote: חַיַּת – לְשׁוֹן עֲרָבִי הוּא: צֹרֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says חית is Arabic and means need.

sources.quote: פי' חית ידך, חיי כחך
sources.says: Radak says חית ידך means the life of your strength.

sources.quote: חית. כמו כח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says חית means strength.

57:11.headline: To lie, or to let down someone who trusted you
57:11.body: כזב usually means to lie. Rashi says it means to fail someone who relied on you, like a spring whose water runs dry. Radak reads it as lying, denying what she did.

sources.quote: מִי שֶׁבּוֹטְחִין עָלָיו וְהוּא כּוֹזֵב וּבוֹגֵד
sources.says: Rashi says כזב describes someone people trust who fails and betrays them.

sources.quote: אם תרצי לכזב ולאמר שלא עשית אלה המעשים
sources.says: Radak reads it as lying, saying she did not do these things.

57:13.headline: When you cry out, or when you call your allies together?
57:13.body: זעק usually means to cry out. Metzudat Zion says here it means to gather, since people are gathered by a call. Radak reads it as crying out for help in trouble.

sources.quote: ענין קבוץ ואסיפה על כי באה בזעקת המאסף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means gathering, because a gathering comes at the call of the one who assembles it.

sources.quote: כשתזעקי מרעת האויבים
sources.says: Radak reads it as when you cry out because of the enemies.

57:15.headline: “High and lifted up” means greatness, not a high place
57:15.body: נשא means lifted up. Maimonides says that when the Bible calls God lifted up, it means greatness and power, not that God is high up in space.

sources.quote: רוממות וגדולה ועוז, לא עילוי מקום
sources.says: Maimonides says that in this verse the word means exaltation, greatness and might, not height of place.

57:15.headline: God “dwells forever”: what dwelling means for God
57:15.body: שכן means to dwell in one place. Radak says a person who stays in a place is called a dweller, so God is called one because his care for his creatures never stops.

sources.quote: כן יקרא האל ית' שוכן עד לפי שמתמיד השגחתו בנבראים
sources.says: Radak says God is called the one who dwells forever because his care for creatures is constant.

57:16.headline: The spirit wraps the body, or the spirit grows faint
57:16.body: עטף can mean to wrap or to grow faint. Radak says the spirit wraps the body and guides it to the good way. Rashi says the spirit grows faint and humble, and then God ends his anger.

sources.quote: והוא יעטוף וילבש הגוף ויכבוש אותו ללכת בדרך הטובה
sources.says: Radak says the spirit wraps and clothes the body and leads it in the good way.

sources.quote: יַעֲטוֹף יוֹדֶה וְיִכָּנַע עַל מַעֲלוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the person grows faint, admits his sin and is humbled.

sources.quote: מגזרת לעני כי יעטף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra ties it to the faint, poor man of Psalm 102.

57:18.headline: God will lead him, or give him rest
57:18.body: ואנחהו can come from נחה, to lead, or from נוח, to rest. Rashi gives both readings, and Radak reads it as leading him on the good path.

sources.quote: אוֹלִיכוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ מַרְפֵּא, אוֹ וְאַנְחֵהוּ לְשׁוֹן הֲנָחָה וּמַרְגּוֹעַ
sources.says: Rashi says it means I will lead him on a path of healing, or else it means rest.

sources.quote: ואנחהו. בדרך הטוב
sources.says: Radak says it means I will lead him on the good path.

57:19.headline: Speech as the fruit of the lips
57:19.body: ניב means speech, but it comes from the word for fruit or produce, תנובה. Metzudat Zion says speech is called this because it is the fruit of the tongue.

sources.quote: והוא מלשון תנובות שדי (דברים ל״ב:י״ג) כי הדבור הוא פרי הלשון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from תנובה, produce, because speech is the fruit of the tongue.

sources.quote: ומלת ניב כמו פרי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word ניב is like fruit.

57:21.headline: “My God,” not “the Lord”: Radak fixes the wording
57:21.body: A nearly identical line closes chapter 48 with the name of the Lord. Radak says here the right text is אלהי, my God, and copies that write the Lord are mistaken.

sources.quote: והספרים שכתוב בהם אמר ה' טעות הוא
sources.says: Radak says the copies that read the Lord said here are a mistake.

58:1.headline: Two words for sin: one for scholars, one for everyone else
58:1.body: Rashi reads “my people” and their פשע, deliberate sin, as the Torah scholars, whose honest mistakes count as deliberate. “The house of Jacob” and their חטאת are ordinary people, whose deliberate sins count only as mistakes.

sources.quote: אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, שֶׁכָּל שִׁגְגָתָם פֶּשַׁע, שֶׁשִּׁגְגַת תַּלְמוּד עוֹלָה זָדוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says these are Torah scholars, whose every error counts as a willful sin.

sources.quote: אֵלּוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ, שֶׁאַף זְדוֹנָם שְׁגָגָה
sources.says: Rashi says the house of Jacob are ordinary people, whose willful sins count as errors.

58:2.headline: Nearness to God means knowing, not standing close
58:2.body: Maimonides says “they desire nearness to God” cannot mean nearness in space. It is the nearness of knowledge: coming to understand God.

sources.quote: כי כל אלה קרבת ידיעה, כלומר השגה של ידע, לא קרבת מקום
sources.says: Maimonides says this verse and others like it speak of nearness of knowledge, not nearness of place.

58:3.headline: Your hard-earned money, or the people who owe you
58:3.body: Radak reads עצביכם as your money, earned with toil (עצבון). Rashi reads it as the people in debt to you, who suffer because of you and whom you press on your fast day.

sources.quote: עצביכם. ממונכם כמו ועצביך בבית נכרי כי הממון יגיע האדם ועצבונו
sources.says: Radak says עצביכם means your money, because money is a man’s toil and labor.

sources.quote: בַּעֲלֵי חוֹב שֶׁלָּכֶם, הַנֶּעֱצָבִים עַל יֶדְכֶם, אַתֶּם נוֹגְשִׂים אוֹתָם בְּיוֹם צֹמְכֶם
sources.says: Rashi reads it as those bound to you by debt, who are pained by you, and whom you press on your fast day.

58:5.headline: Bowing like a reed, or bent like a fishhook
58:5.body: Ibn Ezra says אגמון is a soft plant that droops its head, and Metzudat Zion says it is גמא, reed, with the letters turned around. Rashi says it is a bent hook for catching fish.

sources.quote: כאגמון. צמח רך שישח את ראשו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a soft plant that bows its head.

sources.quote: כאגמון. הוא הפוך מן גמא והוא שם צמח רך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word is גמא reversed, the name of a soft plant.

sources.quote: אַגְמוֹן הוּא כְּמִין מַחַט כָּפוּף, וְצָדִין בּוֹ דָּגִים
sources.says: Rashi says an אגמון is a kind of bent needle used to catch fish.

59:3.headline: נגאלו: not "redeemed" but "stained" with blood
59:3.body: גאל often means to redeem, but Rashi and Metzudat Zion say here it means dirtied, as in the "defiled bread" of Malachi 1:7. Radak and Ibn Ezra add that the word blends two verb forms into one.

sources.quote: נְגֹאֲלוּ. לְשׁוֹן ׳טִנּוּף׳, וְכֵן ״לֶחֶם מְגֹאָל״
sources.says: Rashi says נגאלו means made filthy, as in "defiled bread".

sources.quote: נגאלו. ענין טינוף ולכלוך כמו לחם מגואל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נגאלו means dirt and filth, as in "defiled bread".

sources.quote: נגואלו. מלה מורכבת מבנין נפעל ומבניין שלא נקרא שם פועלו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is built from two verb forms joined together.

sources.quote: ומלת נגאלו מורכבת מן נפעל ופעל שלא נזכר שם פועלו
sources.says: Radak says the word נגאלו combines two verb forms.

59:5.headline: והזורה: an egg warmed until it hatches, or crushed underfoot
59:5.body: Rashi follows the Targum: the egg is warmed until a viper breaks out, and he ties the word to Gideon wringing out the fleece. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as crushed, as in Job's "a foot may crush them".

sources.quote: וְהַזּוּרֶה. תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״מְשַׁחְנָן״, לְשׁוֹן ׳חִמּוּם׳
sources.says: Rashi says the Targum renders it as warming the eggs.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ ״וַיָּזַר אֶת הַגִּזָּה״
sources.says: Rashi compares Gideon, who wrung out the fleece.

sources.quote: והזורה. ענין מעוך להוציא הבלוע וכן כי רגל תזורה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means squeezing to push out what is inside, as in "a foot may crush them".

sources.quote: והוא אומר על ביצי הצפעוני כשהוא זורה ברגל
sources.says: Radak says it speaks of a viper's eggs crushed underfoot.

59:10.headline: "We grope": a word found nowhere else in Scripture
59:10.body: Metzudat Zion says this word has no match elsewhere in Scripture, but the sages use it for a ship scraping the bottom. Radak and Ibn Ezra read it as "we feel our way", like the blind.

sources.quote: נגששה. ענין משוש והנגיעה בדבר ואין לו דמיון במקרא ובדרז״ל בזמן שהספינה גוששת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means feeling and touching, has no match in Scripture, and the sages say "when the ship scrapes".

sources.quote: נגששה כעורים קיר.  כמו נמששה
sources.says: Radak says נגששה is like נמששה, we feel our way.

sources.quote: נגששה. כמו נמשש, ואין רע לו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like "we feel", and has no matching word.

59:10.headline: באשמנים: dark places, graves, or among the well-fed living
59:10.body: Rashi reports that Menachem reads it as dark places, while Dunash reads it from שמן, fat: among the healthy living we are like the dead. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as desolate graves.

sources.quote: מְנַחֵם פָּתַר לְשׁוֹן ׳מַחֲשַׁכִּים׳
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem explains it as dark places.

sources.quote: אֲבָל דּוּנַשׁ פָּתַר בּוֹ לְשׁוֹן ׳שׁוּמָן׳
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash explains it from שומן, fat.

sources.quote: אַף כָּאן בֵּין הָאַשְׁמַנִּים בֵּין הַחַיִּים הַשְּׁמֵנִים אֲנַחְנוּ כַּמֵּתִים
sources.says: Rashi says on that reading: among the fat, healthy living, we are like the dead.

sources.quote: באשמנים. בקברים השוממים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means in desolate graves.

sources.quote: והקברים הם מקום שממה
sources.says: Radak says graves are a place of desolation.

59:13.headline: הרו: conceiving lies, teaching them, or shooting them out
59:13.body: Radak reads הרו as conceiving, like "they conceive trouble" in verse 4, while his father and Metzudat Zion read it as teaching. Rashi reads it as shooting out, as in "He cast into the sea", or as teacher and student.

sources.quote: הרו. כמו הרו עמל הנזכר למעלה
sources.says: Radak says הרו is like "they conceived trouble" mentioned earlier.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי זכרונו לברכה פירש הרו כמו להורות את בני ישראל ששרשו ירה
sources.says: Radak says his father explained הרו as teaching, from the root ירה.

sources.quote: הרו. מלשון הוראה ולימוד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הרו means teaching and instruction.

sources.quote: לִירוֹת וּלְהוֹצִיא. הֹרוֹ לְשׁוֹן ״יָרָה בַיָּם״
sources.says: Rashi says it means to shoot and bring out, as in "He cast into the sea".

sources.quote: הֹרוֹ וְהֹגוֹ – הָרַב וְהַתַּלְמִיד
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: the teacher and the student.

59:19.headline: ויראו: will they fear God's name, or see it?
59:19.body: The spelling allows both. Metzudat Zion reads it as "fear" with a letter missing, and Ibn Ezra brings both readings, "fear" and "see".

sources.quote: ויראו. מלשון יראה והוא חסר יו״ד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ויראו comes from fear and is missing a yod.

sources.quote: י"א שהוא מלשון יראה והוא חסר יו"ד, וי"א כמשמעו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some read it as fear with a missing yod, and some read it as it sounds, "they will see".

sources.quote: וְיִדְחֲלוּן מִמַעֲרְבָא יַת שְׁמָא דַייָ
sources.says: The Targum renders it "they will fear the name of the Lord from the west".

59:21.headline: "My spirit": the gift of prophecy, or a spirit against sin
59:21.body: Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion say רוחי here means prophecy, which will never stop. Radak prefers a spirit of purity that God will put in Israel so they will not sin again.

sources.quote: וטעם רוחי נבואתי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says "my spirit" means my prophecy.

sources.quote: רוחי. כן יקרא הנבואה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says prophecy is called רוחי.

sources.quote: וזהו שאמר רוחי אשר עליך זאת רוח טהרה שאתן בתוכם שלא יחטאו עוד
sources.says: Radak says "my spirit upon you" is a spirit of purity that God will put in them so they sin no more.

6:1.headline: Did King Uzziah die that year, or become a leper?
6:1.body: The verse says 'in the year King Uzziah died'. Rashi and the Targum say it means the year he was struck with leprosy, because a leper is counted as dead; Ibn Ezra says it may also mean he really died.

sources.quote: בשנת מות. כשנצטרע
sources.says: Rashi says 'the year of the death' means when he became a leper.

sources.quote: כי המצורע חשוב כמת
sources.says: Metzudat David says a leper is considered as if dead.

sources.quote: ויתכן להיות כמשמעו, כי בשנה שהתנבא מת עזיהו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may mean what it says: Uzziah died in the year Isaiah prophesied.

6:2.headline: The angels are called "burning ones"
6:2.body: שרפים comes from שרף, to burn. Ibn Ezra says they are named for burning the prophet's lips; Rashi says they came to burn King Uzziah when he went into the Temple to offer incense.

sources.quote: שרפים. קראם שרפים בעבור ששרפו פיו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are called seraphim because they burned his mouth.

sources.quote: וזהו שקראם שרפים שבאו לשרפו
sources.says: Rashi says this is why they are called seraphim: they came to burn Uzziah.

6:2.headline: Wings that stand for hiding
6:2.body: כנף means a wing, but also a cover, as in 'shelter under His wings'. Maimonides says that for angels it always means hiddenness: what causes an angel, its 'face', and what it causes, its 'feet', are both hidden from us.

sources.quote: וכן כל "כנף" שנאמר לגבי המלאכים משמעותו סתר
sources.says: Maimonides says every 'wing' said of angels means hiding.

sources.quote: שסיבת מציאותו – כלומר של המלאך – נסתרת ונעלמת מאוד, והיא "פניו"
sources.says: Maimonides says the cause of the angel's existence is deeply hidden, and that is its 'face'.

6:2.headline: The angels hide feet shaped like a calf's
6:2.body: Rashi says the seraph covers its feet out of modesty before its Maker. He also cites a midrash: angels' feet are like a calf's hoof (Ezekiel 1:7), so they are covered so as not to call up Israel's sin of the golden calf.

sources.quote: כסוי הרגלים לפי שהם ״ככף רגל עגל״ (יחזקאל א:ז), שלא להזכיר לישראל עון העגל
sources.says: Rashi says the feet are covered because they are like a calf's foot, so as not to recall Israel's sin of the calf.

sources.quote: ורז״ל אמרו שלא להזכיר מעשה העגל כי כף רגליהם ככף רגל עגל
sources.says: Metzudat David says the sages explained it as not recalling the calf, since their feet are like a calf's.

6:3.headline: The angels call to each other to start together
6:3.body: Rashi, following the Targum, says each angel asks the others' leave, so that none starts alone and is burned. So they all say 'holy' at once, as the morning prayer puts it.

sources.quote: נוטלין רשות זה מזה, שלא יקדים האחד ויתחיל ויתחיב שרפה
sources.says: Rashi says they take leave of one another, so none goes first and is punished with burning.

sources.quote: קדושה כלם כאחד עונים
sources.says: Rashi quotes the morning prayer: they all answer 'holy' as one.

sources.quote: ומקבלין דין מן דין
sources.says: The Targum says they receive from one another.

6:3.headline: Why "holy" is said three times
6:3.body: The Targum explains each 'holy': in the highest heavens, on earth, and forever. Radak reads the three as three worlds: angels and souls, the stars, and our own world.

sources.quote: קדיש בשמי מרומא עלאה בית שכנתיה קדיש על ארעא עובד גבורתיה קדיש לעלם ולעלמי עלמיא
sources.says: The Targum says: holy in the highest heavens, holy on earth, holy forever.

sources.quote: קדוש קדוש קדוש. שלוש פעמים, כתרגומו
sources.says: Rashi says the three times are explained as the Targum does.

sources.quote: וזכר שלש פעמים קדוש כנגד שלשה עולמות
sources.says: Radak says 'holy' is said three times for three worlds.

6:3.headline: God's "glory" fills the earth: light, or praise?
6:3.body: כבוד can mean a created light, God's very being, or praise. Maimonides says here it means praise: the whole earth shows God's perfection, not that something physical fills it.

sources.quote: כי השיבוח נקרא כבוד
sources.says: Maimonides says praise is called כבוד, and reads this verse that way.

sources.quote: פירוש הדברים: כל הארץ מעידה על שלמותו
sources.says: Maimonides says the verse means the whole earth bears witness to God's perfection.

sources.quote: לא שיש גוף שממלא מקום
sources.says: Maimonides says it does not mean a body filling a place.

6:4.headline: Doorposts measured in cubits, or moved by cubits?
6:4.body: אמות usually means cubits. Rashi, following the Targum, says these are the doorposts, named for being measured in cubits; Ibn Ezra says the posts moved cubits from their place.

sources.quote: הם מזוזות הפתח, שנמדדין במדות אמות לגבה ולרחב
sources.says: Rashi says they are the doorposts, which are measured in cubits.

sources.quote: וטעם אמות, שהספים סרו ממקומם אמות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the doorposts moved cubits from their place.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים כי אין למלה הזאת אחות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that some say this word has no match elsewhere.

6:5.headline: "I am lost" or "I am silenced"?
6:5.body: Rashi reads נדמיתי as 'I am as good as dead' for having seen God. Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra also hear silence in it, as in 'Aaron was silent': one who is lost is silenced.

sources.quote: כי נדמיתי. הריני מת
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'I am dead'.

sources.quote: נדמיתי. ענין שתיקה כמו וידום אהרן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word is about silence, as in 'Aaron was silent'.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים מלשון דמי (תהלים ס"ב ו'), גם הוא נכון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some read it as silence, and that is also right.

6:6.headline: A coal whose spelling says "crush the mouth"
6:6.body: רצפה is a glowing coal, the same word as רשפה with a ש. Rashi says it is spelled with a צ to hint רצוץ פה, 'crush the mouth', because Isaiah had spoken badly of Israel.

sources.quote: ונאמר בישעיהו ובאליהו בצד״י ׳רצפה׳, מפני שאמרו דילטוריא על ישראל
sources.says: Rashi says it is spelled with a צ because Isaiah and Elijah spoke against Israel.

sources.quote: רצוץ פה שאמר דילטוריא על בני
sources.says: Rashi says God told the angel: crush the mouth that spoke against My children.

sources.quote: רצפה. גחלת והוא כמו רשפה בשי״ן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says רצפה is a coal, the same as רשפה with a ש.

6:8.headline: "Who will go for us?" God speaks to the angels
6:8.body: God says 'us', not 'me'. Ibn Ezra and Radak say God is speaking to the seraphim, as if taking counsel with them, like 'let us go down' at Babel.

sources.quote: אומר לשרפים על כן מלת לנו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says God speaks to the seraphim, and that is why it says 'us'.

sources.quote: ואמר לנו לשון רבים כאלו היה מדבר עם השרפים ונמלך עמהם בזה הדבר וכן הבה נרדה
sources.says: Radak says 'us' is plural, as if God were consulting the seraphim, like 'let us go down'.

6:9.headline: An order not to understand, or a people who won't?
6:9.body: Read plainly, God orders the people to hear and not understand, and Radak gives this reading, like God hardening Pharaoh's heart. He and Rashi also read it as a description: you hear the prophets and do not take it in.

sources.quote: יש מפרשים שמעו וראו לשון צווי כמשמעו
sources.says: Radak says some read 'hear' and 'see' as plain commands.

sources.quote: כלומר אתם שומעים באזניכם דברי הנביאים המוכיחים אתכם ואין אתם מבינים
sources.says: Radak's second reading: you hear the prophets rebuke you and do not understand.

sources.quote: אני אומר לכם שמעו שמוע, ואתם אין אתם נותנים לב להבין
sources.says: Rashi says God tells them to listen, and they do not set their hearts to understand.

6:10.headline: A "fat" heart, and where the word for fool comes from
6:10.body: The verse says 'make the heart fat', meaning dull. The Targum renders it טפיש, and Metzudat Zion says this is why a fool is called טפש.

sources.quote: טפיש לביה דעמא הדין
sources.says: The Targum says: the heart of this people is fat.

sources.quote: טפש. ענין שומן כי השמן לב העם הזה (ישעיהו ו׳:י׳) תרגומו טפש לבא ומזה קראו לכסיל טפש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says טפש means fat, as the Targum renders this verse, and from it a fool is called טפש.

6:10.headline: Eyes plastered shut, or turned away?
6:10.body: Rashi and Radak read השע as smeared over, the way plaster is smeared on a wall, so the eyes cannot see. Metzudat Zion reads it as turning away, as in 'turn your gaze from me' (Psalms 39:14).

sources.quote: ועיניו השע. טחים
sources.says: Rashi says it means smeared shut.

sources.quote: כאלו טחו על העין כדי שלא יראו
sources.says: Radak says it is as if something were smeared over the eye so they cannot see.

sources.quote: השע. ענין הסרה כמו השע ממני ואבליגה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means turning away, as in 'turn from me'.

6:13.headline: Ten more kings, or a tenth left behind?
6:13.body: Radak reads עשריה as ten more kings before the exile, from Uzziah's son to Zedekiah. Metzudat David also offers 'a tenth part' that remains, and the Targum reads it as one in ten who are righteous.

sources.quote: כי עוד ימלכו בארץ עשרה מלכים מעת נבואה זו
sources.says: Radak says ten more kings will rule in the land from the time of this prophecy.

sources.quote: או ר״ל תשעה חלקים יהיו אבודים ותשאר חלק עשירי
sources.says: Metzudat David also says it may mean nine parts will be lost and a tenth will remain.

sources.quote: וישתארון בה חד מן עסרא צדיקיא
sources.says: The Targum says one in ten, the righteous, will remain.

6:13.headline: Falling leaves, or a gate of Jerusalem?
6:13.body: Rashi reads שלכת as the season when trees throw off their leaves. Others, and Ibn Ezra, say Shallekhet was a gate of Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 26:16) where these two trees stood.

sources.quote: אשר בעת זמן שלכת שלהן, משליכין עלין שלהן בימי הסתיו
sources.says: Rashi says it is the time when the trees throw off their leaves in autumn.

sources.quote: ויש פותרים: שער שלכת היתה בירושלים
sources.says: Rashi says some explain that Shallekhet was a gate in Jerusalem.

sources.quote: כאלה וכאלון. שנים אילנים היו בשער שלכת והיו חזקים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says these were two strong trees at the Shallekhet gate.

60:1.headline: Your light has come, or your old light has set?
60:1.body: בא usually means 'has come'. But when the sun 'comes' it sets, so Ibn Ezra reads: your old light has set, and God's glory has risen on you instead; Radak gives both readings.

sources.quote: ולפי דעתי שביאת האור הוא חשך, כמו בא ערב ונפסק האור שהיה לך, וזרח עליך כבוד יי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the light's 'coming' is darkness, as when evening comes; your old light stopped and God's glory rose on you.

sources.quote: הגיע זמן ישועתך שהוא לך אורה גדולה
sources.says: Radak says it means the time of your rescue has come, a great light for you.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים כי בא אורך שקע אורך כמו שאמר ובא השמש
sources.says: Radak says some explain it as 'your light has set', as in 'the sun set'.

60:5.headline: "You will see" or "you will be afraid"?
60:5.body: Some read תראי as 'you will fear', and some copies even add a י. Ibn Ezra reads it that way: the fear of someone hit by sudden good news. Radak says it comes from ראה, 'see', and calls the other reading a mistake.

sources.quote: אז תיראי כאדם שיפחד בבא לו תשועה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reads 'you will fear', like a person who is afraid when rescue suddenly comes.

sources.quote: ורבים טעו בזאת המלה שקראו התי"ו בגעיא, כמו מן ירא, וגם יש ספרים שכתוב ביו"ד וטעות הוא כי מן ראה היא
sources.says: Radak says many wrongly read it as from 'fear', and some copies add a י, but it comes from 'see'.

60:5.headline: Will your face shine, or will you run about?
60:5.body: Radak and the Targum read ונהרת as light: your face will glow when you see your children coming. Ibn Ezra reads it as running here and there.

sources.quote: ויצהבו פניך, זהו ונהרת שהוא ענין אורה
sources.says: Radak says your face will glow; ונהרת is a word for light.

sources.quote: בכן תחזין ותנהרין
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum: then you will see and shine.

sources.quote: ונהרת. תרוצי פה ופה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means you will run here and there.

60:6.headline: Young camels, or lambs brought as gifts?
60:6.body: Rashi and the Targum read בכרי as young camels, as in 'a swift young she-camel' (Jeremiah 2:23). Ibn Ezra reads the ב as a prefix and the word as כר, a lamb: they will bring a gift.

sources.quote: הם גמלים בחורים, וכן ״בכרה קלה״
sources.says: Rashi says they are young camels, as in 'a swift young she-camel'.

sources.quote: בכרי. הבי"ת משרת, מגזרת שלחו כר (ישעיהו ט"ז א'), ישאו דורון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the ב is a prefix and the word is כר, 'lamb', as in 'send a lamb'; they will bring a gift.

60:11.headline: Kings led in honor, or led in chains?
60:11.body: נהוגים means 'led'. Radak notes that kings are usually led by their officers in honor; the Targum and Ibn Ezra read it as led in chains: the kings who once led will now be led.

sources.quote: כי מנהג המלכים כשילכו בדרך ילכו רוכבים או רגלים ינהגו אותם שרים דרך כבוד
sources.says: Radak says kings on the road are led by officers as a mark of honor.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם נהוגים זקוקים רוצה לומר אסורים בזיקים
sources.says: Radak says the Targum renders it 'bound', meaning tied in chains.

sources.quote: ומלכיהם. שהיו נוהגים יובאו נהוגים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the kings who used to lead will be brought in, led.

60:12.headline: Laid waste, or put to the sword?
60:12.body: The root חרב can mean ruin or sword. Radak reads ruin and reports others who read killing; Ibn Ezra reads the sword, as in 2 Kings 3:23, and says this is right.

sources.quote: ענין חרבן, ויש מפרשים ענין חרב כלומר יהרגו
sources.says: Radak says it means ruin, and some explain it as the sword, that is, they will be killed.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים מלשון חרבן, והראשון הוא נכון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some read it as ruin, but the first reading, the sword, is right.

60:22.headline: "In its time" and "I will hurry it": which one?
60:22.body: The verse seems to say both: the redemption comes at its set time, and God will rush it. The Talmud answers: if Israel deserves it, God will hurry it; if not, it comes in its time.

sources.quote: כתיב ״בעתה״ וכתיב ״אחישנה״. זכו – אחישנה, לא זכו – בעתה
sources.says: The Talmud says: if they merit it, I will hurry it; if not, in its time.

sources.quote: בעתה אחישנה. זכו – אחישנה, לא זכו – בעתה
sources.says: Rashi gives the same answer.

sources.quote: ויש לפרש כשיגיע עתה אחישנה, לגמרה מהרה
sources.says: Radak also reads it as: when its time comes, I will finish it quickly.

61:1.headline: Anointed with oil, or simply raised to a high post
61:1.body: Rashi says this משיחה is not anointing with oil but a word for authority and greatness. Radak explains: kings were appointed by anointing, so any appointment came to be called anointing, even with no oil.

sources.quote: אֵין מְשִׁיחָה זוֹ, אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן שְׂרָרָה וּגְדֻלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says this is not anointing but a word for rule and greatness.

sources.quote: ולפי שמנוי המלכים הוא על ידי משיחה נאמר למנוי אחר לשון משיחה, ואף על פי שאין שם משיחה
sources.says: Radak says that because kings are appointed by anointing, other appointments are also called anointing, even without oil.

62:4.headline: The land is called 'married', meaning lived in
62:4.body: בעולה means a married woman. Rashi says it means the land will be lived in, and Radak explains the picture: a settled land is like a wife, and an empty one is like a widow.

sources.quote: בְּעוּלָה. מְיֻשֶּׁבֶת
sources.says: Rashi says the word means inhabited.

sources.quote: כי הארץ המיושבת דומה לאשה שיש לה בעל
sources.says: Radak says a settled land is like a woman who has a husband.

62:5.headline: Your children will 'marry' you, meaning settle in you
62:5.body: Read literally, Zion's sons will marry her, which is a strange picture. Rashi quotes the Targum, which reads the verb as settling: as a young man settles with his bride, so your children will settle in you.

sources.quote: כֵּן יִתְיַיתְבִין בְּגַוֵּיכִי בְּנַיְיכִי
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum: so will your children settle within you.

sources.quote: כֵּן יִתְיַתְבוּן בְּגַוַיְכִי בְּנַיְכִי
sources.says: The Targum translates the verb as settling in, not marrying.

62:6.headline: The Targum reads the walls as the forefathers
62:6.body: Rashi notes that the Targum does not take Jerusalem's walls literally. It reads them as the early forefathers, whose merit protects us like a wall.

sources.quote: וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם חוֹמוֹתַיִךְ: אָבוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים, הַמְּגִינִים עָלֵינוּ כַּחוֹמָה
sources.says: Rashi says Jonathan translated 'your walls' as the first fathers, who shield us like a wall.

62:6.headline: Who are the watchmen on Jerusalem's walls?
62:6.body: The sages say the שמרים are angels who keep reminding God to rebuild the city. Ibn Ezra says they are the mourners of Zion, who weep and do not sleep at night.

sources.quote: מַלְאָכִים הַמַּזְכִּירִים אֶת ה׳ עַל חֻרְבָּנָהּ לִבְנוֹתָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says our rabbis explained them as angels who remind God to rebuild the ruined city.

sources.quote: אלה השומרים כנוי על אבלי ציון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the watchmen stand for the mourners of Zion.

62:6.headline: Two words for silence that are not the same
62:6.body: The verse says both לא יחשו and אל דמי. Malbim says חשה is simply not speaking, while דמי means stopping in the middle, so the watchmen may not pause even for a moment.

sources.quote: פעל דום מציין ההפסקה מן הדבור הקודם לו, לא כן חשה מציין העדר הדבור לבד
sources.says: Malbim says דום means breaking off speech already under way, while חשה only means not speaking.

62:8.headline: The Talmud reads God's 'strong arm' as tefillin
62:8.body: The Talmud asks how we know God wears tefillin, and answers from this verse. 'His right hand' is the Torah, and 'the arm of His strength' is tefillin, because another verse calls them strength, עז.

sources.quote: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין
sources.says: The Talmud asks how we know God puts on tefillin, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: וּבִזְרוֹעַ עֻזּוֹ״ — אֵלּוּ תְּפִילִּין
sources.says: The Talmud says 'His right hand' is the Torah and 'the arm of His strength' is tefillin.

62:12.headline: 'Sought after' reverses an old insult
62:12.body: Zion's new name דרושה means 'sought after'. Radak says it answers the old taunt that 'no one seeks her'.

sources.quote: הפך שהיו קוראים לך ציון היא דורש אין לה
sources.says: Radak says the name is the opposite of what they used to call you: Zion, no one seeks her.

63:1.headline: Bozrah sounds like Bezer, the city of refuge
63:1.body: The sages say Edom's angel will think Bozrah protects him because it sounds like Bezer, a city of refuge. He is wrong, since refuge is only for those who kill by accident.

sources.quote: כְּסָבוּר הוּא שֶׁבָּצְרָה הִיא ״בֶּצֶר בַּמִּדְבָּר״ (דברים ד:מג) שֶׁהָיְתָה עִיר מִקְלָט
sources.says: Rashi brings the sages: Edom's angel thinks Bozrah is Bezer in the desert, a city of refuge.

sources.quote: מִשּׁוּם שֶׁאֵין קוֹלֶטֶת אֶלָּא שׁוֹגֵג וְהוּא הָרַג אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵזִיד
sources.says: Rashi says it is a mistake, because refuge protects only one who killed by accident, and Edom killed Israel on purpose.

63:3.headline: Their “lasting strength” is their blood
63:3.body: נצח usually means victory or forever. Here it means blood, because blood is a person's life and strength.

sources.quote: ונקרא הדם נצח לפי שהוא חיי האדם וחזקו
sources.says: Radak says blood is called נצח because it is a person's life and strength.

sources.quote: דָּמָם, שֶׁהוּא תָּקְפּוֹ וְנִצְחוֹנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
sources.says: Rashi says it is their blood, a person's might and victory.

sources.quote: נצחם הוא הדם שבו יחיה האד' נצחו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says נצחם is the blood by which a person lives his span.

63:3.headline: Not redeemed, but stained
63:3.body: גאל usually means to redeem. Here it means to soil or stain, as in “polluted bread” in Malachi. The form is also odd, with an א where you expect a ה.

sources.quote: ואגאלתי ענין טנוף ולכלוך, וכן לחם מגואל
sources.says: Radak says the word means soiling and staining, as in polluted bread.

sources.quote: ענין לכלוך כמו לחם מגואל (מלאכי א׳:ז׳) והאל״ף תחת הה״א
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means soiling, and the א stands in for a ה.

sources.quote: ולפי דעתי שהיא מלה מורכבת מפועל עבר ועתיד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra thinks the word blends a past-tense and a future-tense form.

63:7.headline: חסד: kindness given to someone you owe nothing
63:7.body: Maimonides says חסד means going beyond what is owed. In the prophets it usually means doing good for someone with no claim on you, so every good thing from God is חסד.

sources.quote: השימוש הנפוץ של ספרי הנבואה בביטוי "חסד" הוא לעשיית טוב למי שאין לך כל מחויבות כלפיו
sources.says: Maimonides says the prophets usually use חסד for doing good to someone you have no duty toward.

sources.quote: לכן כל טובה המגיעה ממנו יתעלה נקראת "חסד"
sources.says: Maimonides says this is why every good thing that comes from God is called חסד, citing this verse.

63:9.headline: Written “he did not afflict,” read “he was afflicted”
63:9.body: The text is written לא, not, but read לו, to him. Written, it says God did not let their trouble grow. Read aloud, it says God himself felt their pain.

sources.quote: כתוב באל"ף וקרי בוי"ו, ופי' הכתוב לא הרבה להם הצרה כי הושיעם ממנה, ופי' הקרי לו לאל צר בצרתם
sources.says: Radak says the written form means God did not let the trouble grow, and the read form means God was pained in their pain.

sources.quote: כאלו גם הוא הוה [צ"ל היה] בצרה על כן מהר להושיעם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is as if God too were in trouble, so he hurried to save them.

63:9.headline: “The angel of his presence”: Michael, or a chain of events
63:9.body: Rashi says the angel is Michael, who serves before God. Radak says the angel is the set of causes God arranges to save them, which do not happen by chance.

sources.quote: כִּי מַלְאַךְ פָּנָיו הוּא מִיכָאֵל שַׂר הַפָּנִים
sources.says: Rashi says the angel of his presence is Michael, the prince of the presence.

sources.quote: ומלאך פניו הושיעם מסבב סבות להושיעם והסבות יצאו מלפניו לא שיהו מקרה, והסבה תקרא מלאך
sources.says: Radak says God arranges causes to save them, they come from him and are not chance, and such a cause is called an angel.

63:9.headline: God “lifted them up”: raised in honor, not in height
63:9.body: נשא can mean to lift something higher, or to raise someone in rank. Maimonides lists this verse under the second meaning.

sources.quote: וכן יש ל"נשא" א) משמעות של רום המקום, ב) ומשמעות של רוממות הדרגה ויתרון המעלה
sources.says: Maimonides says נשא can mean height of place or greatness of rank.

sources.quote: ובמשמעות השנייה: "וְתִנַּשֵּׂא מַלְכֻתוֹ" (במדבר כד,ז), "וַיְנַטְּלֵם וַיְנַשְּׂאֵם"
sources.says: Maimonides puts this verse under the second meaning, greatness of rank.

63:10.headline: They “grieved” his spirit: here the word means rebelled
63:10.body: עצב can mean pain, anger, or rebellion and sin. Maimonides says in this verse it means rebellion, so the people defied God's holy spirit.

sources.quote: ג) והוא שמם של המרי והחטא
sources.says: Maimonides says one meaning of עצב is rebellion and sin.

sources.quote: "מָרוּ וְעִצְּבוּ אֶת רוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ" (ישעיהו סג,י)
sources.says: Maimonides gives this verse as his first example of that meaning.

63:15.headline: God's heavenly home, the word behind Zebulun's name
63:15.body: זבול is a rare word for a dwelling. Ibn Ezra ties it to Leah's words when she named Zebulun: יזבלני אישי, now my husband will dwell with me.

sources.quote: מזבול, כמו דירה, וכמוהו יזבלני אישי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says מזבול means a dwelling, like Leah's יזבלני אישי.

sources.quote: מזבול. ענין מדור כמו בית זבול לך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a dwelling, like Solomon's house of זבול for God.

63:15.headline: God's “stirring insides” means the heart
63:15.body: מעים literally means the bowels. Maimonides says the word can mean any inner organ, and here it means the heart, the only inner organ the Bible gives to God.

sources.quote: הוא שם המעיים באופן פרטי, ושם כל אבר פנימי באופן כללי, ועל כן הוא גם שם הלב
sources.says: Maimonides says the word means the bowels in a narrow sense and any inner organ in a broad sense, so it can mean the heart.

sources.quote: מן האברים הפנימיים לא הושאל לו אלא הלב
sources.says: Maimonides says the heart is the only inner organ the Bible borrows to describe God.

63:17.headline: A word built from “harden” and “turn away”
63:17.body: תקשיח is very rare. Metzudat Zion says it joins two words, קשה, hard, and סח, to turn aside. So God hardens our heart and turns it away from fearing him.

sources.quote: היא מלה מורכבת מן קשה ומן סח ר״ל תקשה ותסיח לבנו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a compound of קשה and סח: you harden and turn aside our heart.

sources.quote: ענין אכזריות ורחוק הלב מהדבר הנאהב
sources.says: Radak says it means cruelty, the heart pulling away from what it loves.

63:19.headline: Mountains that flowed, or mountains that trembled
63:19.body: נזל usually means to flow. Metzudat Zion reads it as dripping, and Radak says at Sinai the mountain both shook and dripped water. Rashi reads it as trembling.

sources.quote: נזולו. ענין הטפה כמו יזל מים מדליו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means dripping, like water from buckets.

sources.quote: והנה היה ההר בוער באש ונוזל מים כי האש והענן עליו
sources.says: Radak says the mountain was burning with fire and dripping water, since fire and cloud were on it.

sources.quote: אָז מִפָּנֶיךָ הָרִים נָזֹלּוּ בְּרֶתֶת וְזִיעַ
sources.says: Rashi says the mountains melted in trembling and shaking.

65:4.headline: Spending the night among corpses, or in ruins
65:4.body: נצורים means things shut in. Rashi says it means corpses, locked in the grave as if under siege. Radak and Ibn Ezra say it means ruins, where people slept hoping demons would appear to them.

sources.quote: הֵם פִּגְרֵי הַמֵּתִים, שֶׁהֵם כִּנְתוּנִים בְּמָצוֹר, שֶׁאֵינָם יְכוֹלִים לָצֵאת
sources.says: Rashi says they are corpses, shut in as if under siege and unable to get out.

sources.quote: בחרבות ילינו בלילה שיראו להם השדים לדעתם
sources.says: Radak says they slept in ruins at night so that demons would appear to them, as they believed.

sources.quote: ובנצורים. חרבות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says נצורים means ruins.

65:5.headline: Not “I made you holy” but “I am holier than you”
65:5.body: קדשתיך looks like “I have made you holy.” Rashi and Ibn Ezra say it means “I am holier than you”: the sinners tell others to keep their distance.

sources.quote: וכן הוא כי קדשתי ממך, אני קדוש ממך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means I am holier than you.

sources.quote: כִּי קָדַשְׁתִּי וְטָהַרְתִּי יוֹתֵר מִמְּךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it means I am holier and purer than you.

65:8.headline: Sweet wine in a doomed cluster: Noah in the flood generation
65:8.body: The verse speaks of new wine found in a cluster of grapes. Rashi follows the Targum: the sweet wine is Noah, and the cluster is his generation. He hears שכול, bereaved, in אשכול.

sources.quote: הַתִּירוֹשׁ. זֶה נֹחַ, שֶׁהָיָה מָתוֹק
sources.says: Rashi says the new wine is Noah, who was sweet.

sources.quote: בָּאֶשְׁכּוֹל. בַּדּוֹר הַמְשֻׁכָּל, וְיֵשׁ לִפְתּוֹר כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the cluster is the bereaved generation, though it can also be read literally.

65:11.headline: Meni: a star god, or a count of cups
65:11.body: Radak says Meni is the name of a star, or the seven numbered planets. Rashi reads it from מנה, to count: they filled cups by the number of their priests.

sources.quote: ר"ל נסך למני והוא שם כוכב, ויש מפרשים לככבים שהם מנוים והם שבעה ככבי לכת
sources.says: Radak says Meni is a star, and some say it means the counted stars, the seven planets.

sources.quote: לְמִנְיַן חֶשְׁבּוֹן הַכּוֹמְרִים הָיוּ מְמַלְאִים אֲגָנוֹת מֶזֶג יַיִן
sources.says: Rashi says they filled bowls of mixed wine by the count of the priests.

65:12.headline: You served Meni, so I will number you for the sword
65:12.body: The verse before mentions the god Meni. Now God says ומניתי, I will count you out for the sword. Radak and Ibn Ezra say the prophet plays on the sound on purpose.

sources.quote: ומניתי. לשון נופל על הלשון, והוא דרך צחות
sources.says: Radak says ומניתי is a play of one word on another, a deliberate turn of phrase.

sources.quote: אתם עובדים למנין הככבים ואני אמנה אתכם לחרב ולא יחסר אחד
sources.says: Radak says: you worship the counted stars, and I will count you for the sword, and not one will be missing.

sources.quote: ובעבור שאמר למני אמר אחריו ומניתי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says because the prophet said למני, he followed it with ומניתי.

65:15.headline: Your name will become a curse word
65:15.body: שבועה means an oath. Radak says here it means a curse, because people swear by calling down harm on themselves. The wicked's names will be used that way, “may God kill you as he killed so-and-so.”

sources.quote: לשבועה. כמו לקללה
sources.says: Radak says שבועה here is like a curse.

sources.quote: כי בשבועה יזכיר האדם קללה כמו שאומר אדם בשבועתו אהיה כך וכך אם עשיתי זה
sources.says: Radak says an oath mentions a curse, as when someone swears, may such-and-such happen to me if I did this.

sources.quote: לוֹקֵחַ מִשִּׁמְכֶם קְלָלָה וּשְׁבוּעָה לְדוֹרוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says people will take a curse and an oath from your name for generations.

65:16.headline: Seeking a blessing, or boasting?
65:16.body: התברך can mean to ask a blessing for yourself or to praise yourself. Radak reads it as asking for blessing. Metzudat Zion reads it as boasting, so whoever boasts will boast of the true God.

sources.quote: ופי' מתברך מבקש הברכה לעצמו
sources.says: Radak says מתברך means asking a blessing for oneself.

sources.quote: המתברך. ענין התפארות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means boasting.

65:16.headline: God called “the God of Amen”
65:16.body: Amen comes from the root for faith and truth. Rashi says God is called this because he is true and kept his promise. Ibn Ezra says the whole world will see he is the only true God.

sources.quote: אֱלֹהֵי הָאֱמֶת, שֶׁאִמֵּן וְשָׁמַר הַבְטָחָתוֹ זֹאת
sources.says: Rashi says it means the God of truth, who confirmed and kept this promise.

sources.quote: כי אין אלוה אמת זולתו, כי אמן מגזרת אמונה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says there is no true God but him, and אמן comes from the root of faith.

sources.quote: אמן. ענינו כמו אמת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אמן means truth.

65:17.headline: New heavens: a figure of speech, or really new?
65:17.body: Radak says the world will feel new because life will be so good. Rashi gives a reading about the heavenly rulers being replaced, then says the literal reading is the main one. Maimonides notes that sages who took it literally still said these heavens were made at Creation.

sources.quote: מרוב הטובה שתהיה כאלו יהיה העולם חדש
sources.says: Radak says there will be so much good it will be as if the world were new.

sources.quote: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים (פרקי דרבי אליעזר כא) שָׁמַיִם חֲדָשִׁים מַמָּשׁ, וְכֵן עִקָּר
sources.says: Rashi says some read it as truly new heavens, and that is the main reading.

sources.quote: אף שמים וארץ שעתידין להִברות כבר הן ברויין ועומדין
sources.says: Maimonides cites the sages: even the heavens and earth to be created in the future were already created and stand ready.

65:22.headline: As long as a tree lives, or the tree of life
65:22.body: The verse says my people's days will be like the days of the tree. The Targum, cited by Rashi, reads it as the tree of life. Radak and Ibn Ezra read it as an ordinary long-lived tree, like the carob.

sources.quote: כִּימֵי הָעֵץ. תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: עֵץ הַחַיִּים
sources.says: Rashi says the Targum renders it the tree of life.

sources.quote: כי כימי העץ שיטעו כן יהיו ימיהם
sources.says: Radak says their lives will last as long as the trees they plant.

sources.quote: שיעמוד שנים רבות כמו החרוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a tree that stands many years, like the carob.

66:1.headline: "Heaven is My throne": a sign of greatness, not a seat
66:1.body: Maimonides says כסא first means a chair, then anything that shows a ruler's greatness, like the Temple. The heavens are called God's throne because they point to the greatness of the One who made them, and Radak also says God is not a body that sits.

sources.quote: נקרא המקדש "כסא", כיוון שהוא מורה על גדולתו של מי שהתגלה בו
sources.says: Maimonides says the Temple is called a throne because it shows the greatness of the One revealed in it.

sources.quote: בשל המשמעות הזו נקראו השמים "כסא", משום שהם מורים למי שמכיר אותם ומתבונן בהם על גדולתו של מי שיצרם
sources.says: Maimonides says the heavens are called a throne because, to one who studies them, they show the greatness of their Maker.

sources.quote: ומה שאמר כסאי לא שיהיה הוא יתברך גוף שישב בכסא אלא דרך משל
sources.says: Radak says "My throne" does not mean God is a body sitting on a chair; it is a picture.

66:2.headline: "Trembling at My word" may mean hurrying eagerly toward it
66:2.body: Metzudat Zion says חרד here means great haste, as in "the elders of the town hurried to meet him". Rashi, on the same word in verse 5, says the righteous hurry with trembling to come close to God's word.

sources.quote: וחרד. ענין מהירות רב וכן ויחרדו זקני העיר לקראתו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חרד means great haste, as in "the elders of the town hurried to meet him".

sources.quote: הַצַּדִּיקִים הַמְמַהֲרִים בַּחֲרָדָה לְהִתְקָרֵב אֶל דְּבָרָיו
sources.says: Rashi says these are the righteous who hurry with trembling to draw near to God's words.

sources.quote: ואל החרד על דברי לעשותם
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the one who is eager to do God's words.

66:3.headline: "Blessing" here means a gift: a present of stolen goods
66:3.body: Rashi, Radak and Metzudat Zion say ברכה can mean a gift brought when greeting someone, as Jacob told Esau, "take my blessing". So the one who burns incense is like one who brings God a stolen gift.

sources.quote: מְבָרֵךְ אוֹתִי בִּתְשׁוּרַת אֹנֶס
sources.says: Rashi says it means he "blesses" God with a gift taken by force.

sources.quote: וּלְשׁוֹן ׳בְּרָכָה׳ נוֹפֵל בִּתְשׁוּרָה שֶׁהִיא לְהַקְבָּלַת פָּנִים, כְּמוֹ ״קַח נָא אֶת בִּרְכָתִי״
sources.says: Rashi says the word ברכה is used for a gift brought when greeting someone, as in "take my blessing".

sources.quote: מברך. מביא מנחה כמו קח נא ברכתי שענינו כמו מנחתי
sources.says: Radak says מברך means bringing a gift, as in "take my blessing", which means my gift.

sources.quote: מברך. הוא ענין תשורה הבאה להקבלת פנים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a gift brought when greeting someone.

66:3.headline: Dog and pig look partly clean, like these sacrificers
66:3.body: Radak says the dog and the pig each show some of the signs of a clean animal, yet both are unclean. So too these people show one good deed, bringing an offering, while their deeds are unclean.

sources.quote: והנה שניהם יש בהם צד סימני טהרה והם טמאים, כך הם מראים בעצמם צד מעשה טוב בהקריבם הקרבן והם טמאים במעשיהם הרעים
sources.says: Radak says both animals have some signs of being clean yet are unclean, just as these people show a good deed in bringing an offering but are unclean in their evil deeds.

66:5.headline: יכבד: "God will be honored", or "God is heavy on us"
66:5.body: Rashi reads it as the sinners boasting that God is honored through them. Ibn Ezra reports Rabbi Moshe HaKohen, and Radak agrees, that it means heavy: the sinners say God's commands weigh on them.

sources.quote: בִּגְדֻלָּתֵנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִתְכַּבֵּד
sources.says: Rashi says the sinners claim God is honored by their greatness.

sources.quote: אמר רבי משה הכהן כי הוא מלשון כבדות, והטעם כי הוא כבד עליו לזכרו ולשמר חוקיו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports Rabbi Moshe HaKohen: the word means heaviness, since remembering God and keeping His laws is heavy on them.

sources.quote: כלומר כבד הוא עלינו במצותיו אשר צונו
sources.says: Radak says they mean God is heavy on us with the commands He gave us.

66:9.headline: אשביר: bringing a woman to the birthstool, not "breaking"
66:9.body: Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra say the word comes from משבר, the seat where a woman gives birth. Rashi explains: would God bring a woman to the birthstool and not open her womb, start something and not finish it?

sources.quote: אשביר. מקום מושב היולדת נקרא משבר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the seat of a woman giving birth is called משבר.

sources.quote: האני אשביר. מגזרת במשבר בנים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says אשביר comes from משבר, the birthing place.

sources.quote: הַאֲנִי אָבִיא אֶת הָאִשָּׁה עַל הַמַּשְׁבֵּר וְלֹא אֶפְתַּח רַחְמָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says: would I bring the woman to the birthstool and not open her womb?

sources.quote: שֶׁמָּא אַתְחִיל בְּדָבָר וְלֹא אוּכַל לִגְמוֹר
sources.says: Rashi says it means: would God start something and not be able to finish it?

66:11.headline: מזיז: glory on the move, radiance, or delight?
66:11.body: Ibn Ezra says the word has no match elsewhere and finds a link to זיז שדי far-fetched. Rashi reads it as glory moving toward her, Radak as radiance like זיו, and the Targum as delight.

sources.quote: אמר רבי משה הכהן כמו וזיז שדי (תהלים נ' י"א) והוא מעט רחוק, והנכון שאין רע לו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Rabbi Moshe HaKohen compared זיז שדי, which is a stretch, and the right view is that the word has no match.

sources.quote: מִכָּבוֹד גָּדוֹל הַזָּז וּמְמַשְׁמֵשׁ לָבֹא לָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means great glory moving and about to come to her.

sources.quote: מזיז. ענינו לפי מקומו כמו זיו
sources.says: Radak says that in this place it means like זיו, radiance.

sources.quote: מַחֲמַד יְקָרָהּ
sources.says: The Targum renders it "the delight of her glory".

66:15.headline: להשיב: to pay back in anger, or to set anger ablaze
66:15.body: Rashi reads it as paying back His enemies in fury. Radak's father reads it from שביב, a spark: to kindle God's anger into flame.

sources.quote: לְהָשִׁיב. לְצָרָיו בְּחֵמָה אֶת אַפּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means to return His anger on His enemies in fury.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פירש להשיב להבעיר מן שביב אש
sources.says: Radak says his father explained להשיב as "to set burning", from שביב, a spark of fire.

66:16.headline: God "is judged": He argues His case as party and judge
66:16.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read נשפט as arguing a case: God is both the party and the judge, and lays out His claims against the wicked. Rashi adds that the plain sense is reordered: all flesh is judged by God's fire and sword.

sources.quote: וּלְפִי שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל דִּין וְדַיָּן, נוֹפֵל בּוֹ לְשׁוֹן ׳נִשְׁפָּט׳
sources.says: Rashi says that since God is both party and judge, the word "is judged" fits Him.

sources.quote: וּפְשׁוּטוֹ כִּי בָאֵשׁ ה׳ וְחַרְבּוֹ נִשְׁפָּט כָּל בָּשָׂר
sources.says: Rashi says the plain sense is that by God's fire and sword all flesh is judged.

sources.quote: נשפט. ענין ויכוח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נשפט means arguing a case.

66:17.headline: Those who "make themselves holy": clean outside, foul within
66:17.body: Maimonides reads the verse as people who wash and purify themselves in public but sin in private. Radak says the verb means they present themselves as holy but are not, while Rashi reads it as making plans to worship idols together.

sources.quote: הוא אומר שהם מיטהרים ומתקדשים במקומות גלויים ופתוחים, ואחר כך חוטאים כשהם לבדם בחדרים ובתוך בתיהם
sources.says: Maimonides says they purify and sanctify themselves in open places, then sin when alone in their rooms and homes.

sources.quote: וכן המתקדשים מראים עצמם כקדושים והם טמאים
sources.says: Radak says המתקדשים are those who show themselves as holy but are unclean.

sources.quote: הַמִּתְקַדְּשִׁים. הַמִּזְדַּמְּנִים
sources.says: Rashi says המתקדשים means those who make appointments with each other.

sources.quote: המתקדשים. ענין הזמנה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says המתקדשים means preparing or setting a meeting.

66:17.headline: "One after another in the middle": groups, a pool, or a tree?
66:17.body: Rashi and the Targum read it as group after group taking turns at an idol in the garden. Radak reads it as the great pool in the middle of the garden, Ibn Ezra as one sacred tree, and Maimonides as a hint of forbidden unions in private.

sources.quote: כְּמָה שֶׁתִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״סִיעָה בָּתַר סִיעָה״
sources.says: Rashi follows the Targum: group after group.

sources.quote: אחר הבריכה הגדולה המיוחדת שהיא בתוך הגן
sources.says: Radak says it means after the one great pool in the middle of the garden.

sources.quote: אשרה אחת, וכתיב אחד והנה הוא עץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means one Asherah, and the written form אחד shows it is a tree.

sources.quote: וייתכן שהוא רומז באומרו "אַחַר אַחַת בַּתָּוֶךְ" להתייחדות ביחסי מין אסורים
sources.says: Maimonides says these words may hint at being alone together in forbidden relations.

66:20.headline: כרכרות: joyful dancing, swift camels, or lambs?
66:20.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as joyful dancing, as David danced (מכרכר). Radak says they are camels or swift beasts that seem to dance as they run, and Rashi reports Menachem's reading from כר, a lamb.

sources.quote: בְּשִׁיר מְשַׂחֲקִים וּמְכַרְכְּרִים, כְּמוֹ ״וְדָוִד מְכַרְכֵּר״
sources.says: Rashi says it means with song, playing and dancing, as "David danced".

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם פֵּרְשׁוֹ לְשׁוֹן ׳כֶּבֶשׂ׳
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem explained it as lambs.

sources.quote: ובכרכרות. ברקודים של שמחה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means with dances of joy.

sources.quote: הם הגמלים או שאר בהמה שהם קלים בהליכתם עד שמרוב מרוצתם ידמה שהם מרקדים
sources.says: Radak says they are camels or other swift animals that seem to dance as they run.

66:21.headline: Hidden priests found again, or nations serving the priests?
66:21.body: Rashi says God knows which of the returning people are really priests and Levites, and will pick them out. Radak's father reads it differently: some of the nations will serve the priests, cutting wood and drawing water.

sources.quote: וּלְפָנַי גְּלוּיִים הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם שֶׁבָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the priests and Levites among them are known to God.

sources.quote: אותם שהיו כבר ממשפחות כהונה ולויה
sources.says: Radak says these are people who were already from priestly and Levite families.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פירש וגם מהם אקח לכהנים ללוים לצורך הכהנים להיות להם חוטבי עצים ושואבי מים
sources.says: Radak says his father explained that God will take some of them for the priests' needs, to cut wood and draw water.

66:22.headline: "New heavens": the same sky, which never grows old?
66:22.body: Radak says the heavens are called new because they never wear out and stay as they were on the day they were made. Ibn Ezra says these heavens will not wear out the way the earlier ones did.

sources.quote: קראם חדשים כי הם עומדים בחדושם ולא יבלו כמו שהיו ביום שנבראו כן הם היום
sources.says: Radak says they are called new because they stay new and do not wear out; as they were the day they were made, so they are today.

sources.quote: עומדים לפני. שלא יבלו כקדמונים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they will stand and not wear out like the former ones.

66:24.headline: דראון: disgrace, "enough seeing", or a worm in the grain
66:24.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as disgrace, while the Targum splits it into two words, "enough seeing": the righteous will say "we have seen enough". Radak traces it to the sages' word for a grain worm, הדרא.

sources.quote: דֵרָאוֹן. לְשׁוֹן ׳בִּזָּיוֹן׳, וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם כְּמִין שְׁתֵּי תֵיבוֹת: דֵּי רְאִיָּה
sources.says: Rashi says דראון means disgrace, and the Targum reads it as two words, "enough seeing".

sources.quote: עַד דְיֵימְרוּן עֲלֵיהוֹן צַדִיקַיָא מִיסַת חֲזֵינָא
sources.says: The Targum says: until the righteous say of them, "we have seen enough".

sources.quote: דראון. ענין בזיון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says דראון means disgrace.

sources.quote: ועקר מלת דראון היא תולעת מלשון רבותינו ז"ל הדרא והכנה שבתבואה
sources.says: Radak says the root sense of דראון is a worm, from the sages' word הדרא for the bug in grain.

7:2.headline: Why forest trees? Because the barren ones rustle loudest
7:2.body: Rashi, citing Bereshit Rabbah, says trees without fruit make more noise than fruit trees. Radak adds that in a forest each tree knocks the next, just as each frightened man frightened the next.

sources.quote: קוֹל אִילָנֵי סְרָק יִשָּׁמַע יוֹתֵר מִכָּל אִילָנֵי פֵּירֵי
sources.says: Rashi says the sound of fruitless trees is heard more than that of fruit trees.

sources.quote: ואחד מניע חברו שנוגע בו מפני התנועה
sources.says: Radak says in a forest one tree shakes the tree next to it.

sources.quote: כן היו כל אחד מהם פוחדים והאחד מפחיד
sources.says: Radak says so each of them was afraid, and each one frightened the other.

7:3.headline: The prophet's son is named 'A remnant will return'
7:3.body: Radak says Isaiah's son was named שאר ישוב as a sign that some of Judah would come back from exile. Rashi and the Targum read it as the few who turn back to God through Isaiah, whom the Targum calls his students.

sources.quote: האחד שמו שאר ישוב לאות ולסימן כי שאר יהודה ישובו עוד אחר הגלות
sources.says: Radak says one son was named Shear-yashuv as a sign that the remnant of Judah would return after exile.

sources.quote: שְׁאֵרִית מְעַט שֶׁיָּשׁוּבוּ אֵלַי עַל יָדְךָ, וְהֵם כְּבָנֶךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the small remnant who will return to God through Isaiah, and they are like his sons.

sources.quote: וּשְׁאָר תַּלְמִידָךְ דְלָא חֲטוֹ וּדְתָבוּ מֵחֶטְאָה
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'the rest of your students, who did not sin and who turned back from sin'.

7:3.headline: The Launderer's Field, where a king hid his face
7:3.body: Plainly it is the field where launderers spread out clothes to dry. The Talmud hears in כובס the word כבש: King Ahaz was ashamed before Isaiah and passed him with his face covered.

sources.quote: שָׂדֶה שֶׁהַכּוֹבְסִים שׁוֹטְחִים שָׁם בְּגָדִים לְנַגְּבָם
sources.says: Rashi says it is a field where launderers spread clothes to dry.

sources.quote: מַאי ״כּוֹבֵס״? אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: דְּכַבְשִׁינְהוּ לְאַפֵּיהּ וַחֲלַף
sources.says: The Talmud asks what כובס hints at, and one view says Ahaz covered his face and passed by.

sources.quote: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ בּשֶׁת פָּנִים מִישַׁעְיָהוּ
sources.says: The Talmud says Ahaz was ashamed before Isaiah.

7:4.headline: 'Be careful', or 'settle down like wine on its lees'?
7:4.body: Rashi, Ibn Ezra and Radak hear שמרים, the dregs wine settles on: sit still, like wine resting on its lees. The Targum and Saadia read the usual 'guard yourself'.

sources.quote: שֵׁב בְּשָׁלוֹם כְּיַיִן עַל שְׁמָרָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it means sit in peace like wine on its lees.

sources.quote: השמר. מלרע מגזרת שמרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is stressed on the last syllable, so it comes from שמרים, the dregs.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם ענין שמירה כלומר אסתמר, וכן פירש רבינו סעדיה
sources.says: Radak says the Targum and Saadia read it as 'guard yourself'.

7:4.headline: Two smoking stubs: these kings can only make smoke
7:4.body: Radak says an אוד is a stick for stirring a fire, and its 'tail' is the burnt stub thrown aside. It smokes but cannot light anything, and so these two kings can frighten but not destroy.

sources.quote: האוד הוא עץ שמנדדין בו האש
sources.says: Radak says an אוד is a stick used to stir the fire.

sources.quote: וכמו שזנב האוד אין בו כח להבעיר דבר אלא שהוא עשן
sources.says: Radak says the stub of the stick has no power to burn, it only smokes.

sources.quote: כִּזְנָבוֹת אוּדִים שֶׁכָּבְתָה שַׁלְהֶבֶת שֶׁלָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says they are like firebrand stubs whose flame has gone out.

7:6.headline: Stir Judah to war, or make it sick of us?
7:6.body: Rashi reads the word from 'wake': we will stir Judah up with war. Metzudat Zion reads it from 'loathe', as in Genesis 27:46: we will besiege it until its people are sick of us and open the gates.

sources.quote: וּנְקִיצֶנָּה. נְעוֹרְרָהּ בְּמִלְחָמָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means we will rouse it with war.

sources.quote: ונקיצנה. ענין מאוס כמו קצתי בחיי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means loathing, as in 'I am disgusted with my life'.

sources.quote: נעשה לה מצור עד שיקיצו מפנינו ויפתחו לנו
sources.says: Radak says they will besiege it until its people loathe them and open the gates.

7:6.headline: Break through its walls, or make it level with us?
7:6.body: Radak says it means breaking through Jerusalem's walls. Rashi and the Targum read it from בקעה, a flat valley: make Judah level with us, under one king with the ten tribes.

sources.quote: נבקיע חומותיה ונכנס בה
sources.says: Radak says they will break through its walls and enter.

sources.quote: נְשַׁוֶּה אוֹתָהּ עִמָּנוּ כְּבִקְעָה זוֹ שֶׁהִיא שָׁוָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means making Judah equal with them, like a flat valley.

sources.quote: וּנְשַׁוִינוּן עִמָנָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'and we will make them equal with us'.

7:6.headline: Tabeel: 'good to us', a code name, or a real name?
7:6.body: The Targum reads טבאל as 'the one who is good to us', and Rashi adds a letter code that turns it into רמלא, pointing at Remaliah's son. Ibn Ezra calls the code nonsense and says it is just the name of an officer.

sources.quote: בֶּן הַטּוֹב אֵלֵינוּ, כֵּן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן
sources.says: Rashi says it means the son who is good to us, as the Targum renders it.

sources.quote: טָבְאַל הוּא רַמְלָא
sources.says: Rashi says that by a letter-swap code טבאל becomes רמלא.

sources.quote: יַת מַן דְכָשַׁר לָנָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'the one who is fit for us'.

sources.quote: והנכון שהוא שם שר גדול מישראל או מארם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra rejects the code reading and says it is the name of a great officer from Israel or Aram.

7:8.headline: Sixty-five years, counted from Amos's prophecy
7:8.body: Ephraim was exiled long before sixty-five years had passed from Isaiah's words. So Rashi and Radak count from Amos's earlier prophecy that Israel would go into exile.

sources.quote: וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִמְנוֹת בְּעוֹד שִׁשִּׁים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה מִיּוֹם שֶׁאָמַר יְשַׁעְיָה נְבוּאָה זוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the sixty-five years cannot be counted from the day Isaiah said this prophecy.

sources.quote: בהשלמות ששים וחמש שנה מנבואת עמוס
sources.says: Radak says it means when sixty-five years are complete from Amos's prophecy.

7:9.headline: Trust, or you will not stand: one root, two meanings
7:9.body: The verse uses the root אמן twice. If you do not trust (תאמינו), you will not last (תאמנו): Radak and Metzudat Zion say the second word means standing firm.

sources.quote: תאמנו. ענין קיום כמו מימיו נאמנים
sources.says: Radak says תאמנו means lasting, as in 'his waters are sure'.

sources.quote: תאמנו. ענין קיום
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means lasting.

sources.quote: אֲרֵי לָא תִתְקַיְמוּן
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'for you will not endure'.

7:11.headline: 'Ask deep': a sign from the depths or the heavens
7:11.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra read שאלה as a command form of 'ask', like שמעה, 'hear', in Daniel 9:19. Rashi says a sign from the deep would be bringing a dead person back to life.

sources.quote: הַעֲמֵק וּשְׁאַל שְׁאָלָה, כְּמוֹ ״שְׁמָעָה סְלָחָה״
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'go deep and ask', a form like 'hear, forgive'.

sources.quote: שְׁאַל אוֹת בְּעִמְקֵי תְהוֹם לְהַחֲיוֹת לְךָ מֵת
sources.says: Rashi says: ask for a sign in the depths, to bring a dead person to life for you.

sources.quote: ומלת שאלה על משקל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word has the same form as שמעה in Daniel 9:19.

7:12.headline: 'I will not test God', or 'I will not raise Him high'?
7:12.body: אנסה usually means 'test'. Metzudat Zion reads it from נס, a tall banner pole: Ahaz refuses to raise God's name high, and Rashi says he did not want God's name made holy through him.

sources.quote: מל׳ נס וענינו התנשאות ורוממות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from נס and means lifting up and exalting.

sources.quote: ולא ארומם את המקום בעשיית האות
sources.says: Metzudat David says Ahaz meant he would not exalt God by having a sign done.

sources.quote: אֵין רְצוֹנִי שֶׁיִּתְקַדֵּשׁ שְׁמוֹ עַל יָדִי
sources.says: Rashi says Ahaz did not want God's name made holy through him.

7:14.headline: Already pregnant, or about to conceive?
7:14.body: Rashi says הרה here speaks of the future, as when the angel told Samson's mother she would conceive. Radak reads it as the present: she is pregnant now and will give birth.

sources.quote: הָרָה. לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says the word speaks of the future, as in Judges 13.

sources.quote: אמר עתה היא הרה ועתה היא יולדת בן
sources.says: Radak says: she is now pregnant and is now about to give birth.

7:14.headline: 'You will call him', or 'she will call him'?
7:14.body: וקראת can look like 'you will call'. Ibn Ezra and Radak say the young mother names him, since mothers then named their children, and Rashi says the holy spirit will rest on her.

sources.quote: וקראת. העלמה כמו וחטאת עמך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the subject is the young woman, a form like 'and your people sinned' in Exodus 5:16.

sources.quote: וקראת. על אמו הוא אומר והיה מנהגם כי האמות היו קוראות שם לבניהן
sources.says: Radak says it speaks of the mother, since mothers used to name their sons.

sources.quote: רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ תִּשְׁרֶה עָלֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says the holy spirit will rest on her.

7:15.headline: Butter and honey: a sign in the baby, or a rich land?
7:15.body: Rashi says the land will be so full that the child eats butter and honey. Ibn Ezra and Radak say the sign is the baby himself: from birth he eats sweet food and refuses bad food.

sources.quote: שֶׁתְּהֵא אַרְצֵנוּ מְלֵאָה כָּל טוּב
sources.says: Rashi says it means our land will be full of good things.

sources.quote: ולפי דעתי שהאות חמאה ודבש יאכל, כי אין מנהג הילדים שיאכלו בעת לדתם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the sign is that he eats butter and honey, since babies do not eat such food when born.

sources.quote: ואם יקריבו לפניו מאכל רע ימאסנו ויסגור פיו לו
sources.says: Radak says that if bad food is brought to the baby, he will refuse it and close his mouth.

7:17.headline: 'Your father's house' is a polite way of saying 'your son'
7:17.body: Rashi, Radak and Metzudat David say the words point to Hezekiah, Ahaz's son. Because Hezekiah was righteous and Ahaz was wicked, the verse does not call him Ahaz's son.

sources.quote: ועל בית אביך. זהו חזקיה בנו ולפי שאחז היה רשע וחזקיה היה צדיק לא קראו בנו
sources.says: Metzudat David says this is Hezekiah his son, not called 'his son' because Ahaz was wicked and Hezekiah righteous.

sources.quote: ולא אמר על בנך לכבוד חזקיהו שהיה צדיק ואחז היה רשע
sources.says: Radak says the verse did not say 'your son' out of respect for Hezekiah.

sources.quote: וּלְפִי שֶׁהוּא צַדִּיק לֹא קְרָאוֹ בְּנוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says because Hezekiah was righteous, the verse did not call him Ahaz's son.

7:19.headline: A word found only here: worthless brush, or houses of praise?
7:19.body: Ibn Ezra says no other word is like הנהלולים. Metzudat Zion says it is low, worthless shrubs, while the Targum, quoted by Rashi, reads it as 'houses of praise'.

sources.quote: גם אין אח למלת הנהלולים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word נהלולים has no sibling anywhere.

sources.quote: שם אילני סרק פחותים ונבזים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the name of low, worthless fruitless trees.

sources.quote: הַנַּהֲלֹלִים. ״בָּתֵּי תוּשְׁבַּחְתָּא״
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum, which renders it 'houses of praise'.

7:19.headline: Thornbushes, which the Talmud reads as idols
7:19.body: Metzudat Zion says נעצוצים are a kind of thornbush. The Talmud reads 'instead of the thornbush' in Isaiah 55:13 as Haman, who made himself an idol, and points to this verse for that sense.

sources.quote: הנעצוצים. מין קוצים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a kind of thorn.

sources.quote: תַּחַת הָמָן הָרָשָׁע שֶׁעָשָׂה עַצְמוֹ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
sources.says: The Talmud says the thornbush stands for wicked Haman, who made himself an idol, citing this verse.

7:20.headline: The beard stands for the king, or a real singed beard
7:20.body: Radak says the beard stands for the king of Assyria himself. The Talmud, as Rashi notes, tells it literally: fire caught in Sennacherib's beard and he shaved it off.

sources.quote: והזקן כנוי למלך
sources.says: Radak says the beard is a figure for the king.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ: גִּלּוּחַ מַמָּשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says the rabbis took it as real shaving.

sources.quote: אִתְּלִי בֵּיהּ נוּרָא בְּדִיקְנֵיהּ. אֲזַל גַּזְיֵיהּ לְרֵישֵׁיהּ וְדִיקְנֵיהּ
sources.says: The Talmud tells that fire caught in his beard, and he shaved his head and beard.

7:21.headline: Two sheep already count as a flock
7:21.body: The Talmud asks how many sheep count as 'many'. Beit Shammai say two, because this verse calls two sheep צאן, and Beit Hillel say five.

sources.quote: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: שְׁתֵּי רְחֵלוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״יְחַיֶּה אִישׁ עֶגְלַת בָּקָר וּשְׁתֵּי צֹאן״
sources.says: Beit Shammai say two ewes are enough, citing this verse.

sources.quote: תַּרְתֵּי נָמֵי אִיקְּרוֹ ״צֹאן״
sources.says: The Talmud explains Beit Shammai: even two are called צאן.

7:23.headline: Costly vineyards left to thorns: a curse, or a sign of devotion?
7:23.body: Rashi says owners flee and their costly vines grow thorns. Metzudat David, like the Talmud, says Hezekiah's generation let the vines go wild because they turned to Torah and gave up wine.

sources.quote: כִּי יַנִּיחוּם בַּעֲלֵיהֶם וּבוֹרְחִין
sources.says: Rashi says their owners will leave them and flee.

sources.quote: כי דורו של חזקיה הרבו לעסוק בתורה וחדלו מן היין
sources.says: Metzudat David says Hezekiah's generation studied Torah a great deal and stopped drinking wine.

sources.quote: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֶלֶף גֶּפֶן בְּאֶלֶף כָּסֶף, לַשָּׁמִיר וְלַשַּׁיִת יִהְיֶה
sources.says: The Talmud applies the verse to Hezekiah's generation: even vines worth a thousand silver pieces were left to thorns.

8:1.headline: Write it so anyone can read it, or write it for real
8:1.body: Rashi says בחרט אנוש, “with a man's pen”, means plain writing that any ordinary person can read quickly. Radak says it means a real human pen: Isaiah must actually write it, not only see it in a vision.

sources.quote: בְּמִכְתָּב כְּתָב אֲשֶׁר יָרוּץ כָּל אֱנוֹשׁ הַקּוֹרֵא בּוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ אֱנוֹשׁ כָּל שֶׁהוּא
sources.says: Rashi says it is writing that any person can run through as he reads, even someone with no learning.

sources.quote: שלא יחשוב כי זה שצוה לו לכתוב במראה הנבואה לבד אלא שיעשה כן ממש
sources.says: Radak says it tells Isaiah not to think the writing happened only in the vision, but to really do it.

8:3.headline: A baby named for how fast the plunder will come
8:3.body: Isaiah's son is named מהר שלל חש בז, “quick spoil, fast plunder.” Rashi says the name foretells the fall of the kings attacking Judah. Radak says the boy was called by one half of the name or the other, not all four words at once.

sources.quote: וִישַׁעְיָה אָבִיו קָרָא שְׁמוֹ ״מַהֵר שָׁלָל״ עַל שֵׁם פֻּרְעָנוּת הָעֲתִידָה לָבֹא עַל רְצִין וּבֶן רְמַלְיָהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says Isaiah named him for the punishment coming on Retzin and the son of Remaliah.

sources.quote: לא נקרא שם הנער בד' תיבות האלה כאחד אלא אמר שיקראו שמו מהר שלל או חש בז
sources.says: Radak says the boy was not called by all four words together, but sometimes מהר שלל and sometimes חש בז.

8:3.headline: The prophetess: a prophet herself, or a prophet's wife
8:3.body: Isaiah's wife is called הנביאה, the prophetess. Radak says she has the title because she was married to a prophet. Ibn Ezra allows that she may have been a prophet in her own right.

sources.quote: היא אשתו וקראה נביאה לפי שהיתה אשת נביא
sources.says: Radak says she was his wife, called a prophetess because she was a prophet's wife.

sources.quote: ונקראה כן בעבור שבעלה נביא, או גם היא היתה נביאה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says she was called this because her husband was a prophet, or because she too was a prophet.

8:8.headline: Up to the neck means up to Jerusalem
8:8.body: The Assyrian flood reaches the neck, so the land nearly drowns. The Targum says the neck is Jerusalem, and Radak explains: the city is the head, and a little more water would have covered it.

sources.quote: עַד יְרוּשְׁלֵם יִמְטֵי
sources.says: The Targum translates it: it will reach as far as Jerusalem.

sources.quote: המשיל ירושלם לראש הגוף, וכשהמים מגיעים לאדם עד צוארו הנה הוא קרוב לטבוע בהם
sources.says: Radak says Jerusalem is pictured as the head, and water up to the neck means a person is close to drowning.

8:8.headline: The verse speaks to Immanuel, “God is with us”
8:8.body: The verse ends by speaking to עמנו אל, “God is with us,” the child's name from chapter 7. Radak says it speaks to that child, a sign that Jerusalem will not fall. Rashi says it means the tribe of Judah, whom God promised to be with.

sources.quote: ואמר עמנו אל שהוא הבן הנולד לאחז, לאות כי לא תכבש
sources.says: Radak says Immanuel is the son born to Ahaz, a sign that the city will not be captured.

sources.quote: הוּא שֵׁבֶט יְהוּדָה, שֶׁהִבְטִיחוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִהְיוֹת עִמָּם
sources.says: Rashi says Immanuel here is the tribe of Judah, whom God promised to be with.

8:19.headline: The mediums do not speak, they chirp like birds
8:19.body: צפצף is the sound a bird makes. Rashi says the word mocks the mediums: they cannot even talk, they just twitter like birds.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן גְּנַאי הוּא, שֶׁאַף הַדִּבּוּר אֵין בָּהֶם, אֶלָּא כְּעוֹפוֹת הַלָּלוּ שֶׁמְּפַטְפְּטִין בְּקוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word of scorn: they have no speech at all, only bird chatter.

sources.quote: כן נקרא השמעת קול העוף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says this is the word for the sound a bird makes.

8:20.headline: A call back to the Torah, or an oath “by the Torah”
8:20.body: Rashi reads לתורה ולתעודה as the answer to give: hold on to the teaching. Radak reads it as an oath, the way a person swears “by the Torah,” while Ibn Ezra says Scripture has no other oath like it.

sources.quote: זוֹ תְּהֵא תְּשׁוּבַתְכֶם, שֶׁתִּשְׁמְרוּ אֶת הַתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says this is your answer: keep the Torah.

sources.quote: לתורה ולתעודה. שבועה כאדם האומר בתורה יהיה כך וכך
sources.says: Radak says it is an oath, like a person who says “by the Torah, this will happen.”

sources.quote: ויש אומרים כי טעם 'לתורה' שבועה, וכדבר הזה לא ראינו במקרא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports those who read it as an oath, but says Scripture has nothing like it.

8:21.headline: Cursing his king, or cursing his idol
8:21.body: Radak reads מלכו as his king, who has no power to save him from hunger. The Targum renders it with a word for an idol.

sources.quote: וקלל במלכו שאין לו כח להושיעו
sources.says: Radak says he curses his king, who has no power to save him.

sources.quote: וְיִבְזֵי שׁוּם פְּתַכְרֵיהּ וְטַעֲוָתֵיהּ
sources.says: The Targum renders it: he will scorn the name of his idol and his false god.

sources.quote: ופתכריה ענין עכו"ם, וכן תרגם סכות מלככם
