sources.says: Radak says the Targum's word פתכריה means an idol, and that it translates “your king” in Amos the same way.

8:23.headline: Made it heavy, or swept it clean
8:23.body: הקל and הכביד make a pair: the first exile was light, the last was heavy. Rashi also reads הכביד as “swept,” like sweeping out a house, because the last exile took everyone.

sources.quote: טִיאֵט אֶת הַכֹּל כִּמְכַבֵּד אֶת הַבַּיִת, וְיֵשׁ לְפָרְשׁוֹ אַף לְשׁוֹן כֹּבֶד
sources.says: Rashi says it means he swept everything away, like sweeping a house, and can also mean heaviness.

sources.quote: המגלה אותה והוא סנחריב הכביד עליהם והגלה אותם שאר השבטים
sources.says: Radak says the last one, Sennacherib, pressed heavily on them and exiled the rest of the tribes.

9:2.headline: Written "not", read "to him": a joy that was not whole
9:2.body: The text is written לא 'not' but read לו 'to him'. Rashi says the spelling hints that Hezekiah's joy was not complete. Ibn Ezra reads the written form as 'there was no joy like it'.

sources.quote: וְכָתִיב ״לֹא״ בְּלָמֶ״ד אָלֶ״ף, לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה שִׂמְחַת חִזְקִיָּה שְׁלֵמָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is written with an aleph because Hezekiah's joy was not complete.

sources.quote: ואשר הוא באל"ף לא היתה שמחה כמוה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the form with aleph means there was no joy like it.

sources.quote: לו לגוי הרבית השמחה אבל לאויביהם לא הגדלת
sources.says: Radak says God increased joy for the nation but not for its enemies.

9:5.headline: Why rule rests on his shoulder
9:5.body: Radak asks why the verse puts rule on the shoulder, when the shoulder usually carries a load. His answer: Ahaz carried Assyria's yoke on his shoulder, but this child will carry rule instead. Rashi says he carries God's yoke there.

sources.quote: למה אמר שכמו לענין משרה, והלא לא נזכר שכמו אלא לענין עבודה
sources.says: Radak asks why the shoulder is used for rule, when it is usually named for labor.

sources.quote: כי זה הילד לא תהיה עבודה על שכמו אלא משרה
sources.says: Radak says this child will carry rule on his shoulder, not servitude.

sources.quote: וְתִהְיֶה מִשְׂרַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְעֻלּוֹ עַל שִׁכְמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says God's rule and yoke will be on his shoulder.

9:6.headline: A closed mem in the middle of a word
9:6.body: In למרבה the mem is written in its closed final form, though it sits mid-word. The Talmud says God wanted to make Hezekiah the Messiah, and the door closed. Radak says the closed letter waits to open when the Messiah comes.

sources.quote: מִפְּנֵי מָה כׇּל מֵם שֶׁבְּאֶמְצַע תֵּיבָה פָּתוּחַ, וְזֶה סָתוּם
sources.says: The Talmud asks why every mem in the middle of a word is open, but this one is closed.

sources.quote: בִּיקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת חִזְקִיָּהוּ מָשִׁיחַ
sources.says: The Talmud answers that God wanted to make Hezekiah the Messiah.

sources.quote: ואז תפתח המשרה שהיא סתומה עד מלך המשיח
sources.says: Radak says the rule that is closed now will open in the time of the Messiah.

sources.quote: כי המ"ם סגור בתוך המלה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra notes the closed mem inside the word and cites the sages' reading.

9:7.headline: A word of prophecy, or the law of the sinew?
9:7.body: Rashi reads דבר as a prophecy of punishment sent to Israel. The Talmud reads it as a rule given to Jacob: the sinew of the thigh, which then spread to all of Israel.

sources.quote: הַנְּבוּאָה שֶׁנִּתְנַבָּא לְפֻרְעָנוּת פֶּקַח
sources.says: Rashi says the 'word' is the prophecy of punishment against Pekah.

sources.quote: ״דָּבָר שָׁלַח בְּיַעֲקֹב״ – זֶה גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה
sources.says: The Talmud says the word sent to Jacob is the law of the sinew of the thigh.

9:15.headline: Those who guide, or those who praise?
9:15.body: אשר can mean to praise someone as happy, or to step and lead. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read 'the guides of this people', from 'my foot held to his steps'. The Targum reads 'those who praise this people'.

sources.quote: מְאַשְּׁרֵי. מַדְרִיכֵי, כְּמוֹ ״בַּאֲשֻׁרוֹ אָחֲזָה רַגְלִי״
sources.says: Rashi says it means guides, as in 'my foot held to his steps'.

sources.quote: מאשרי. מדריכי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means those who guide.

sources.quote: וַהֲווֹ מְשַׁבְּחֵי עַמָא הָדֵין מַטְעָן
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'those who praise this people lead them astray'.

9:17.headline: A strange word for smoke rolling upward
9:17.body: Ibn Ezra calls ויתאבכו a strange word. He and Metzudat Zion read it as rising up, and Metzudat Zion says it has no match. Rashi traces it to נבך, being tangled and trapped in the smoke.

sources.quote: ויתאבכו. מלה זרה כמו התרוממו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a strange word meaning they rose up.

sources.quote: ויתאבכו. הוא ענין התרוממות ואין לו דומה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means rising and has no match.

sources.quote: יִהְיוּ נְבוּכִים וּמְסֻגָּרִים בְּחֹזֶק עֲשַׁן הַתְּבֵעָרָה
sources.says: Rashi says they will be confused and shut in by the thick smoke of the fire.

9:18.headline: Scorched, darkened, or decreed? A word with no twin
9:18.body: The Targum reads נעתם as 'scorched'. Rashi finds that hard, notes the word has no match, and reads 'decreed upon' the land. Ibn Ezra and Radak read it from Arabic as 'darkened'.

sources.quote: וְאַחֲרֵי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן בַּמִּקְרָא
sources.says: Rashi says the word has no parallel in Scripture.

sources.quote: וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן ׳נִגְזַר׳ עַל הָאָרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says it means decreed upon the land.

sources.quote: נעתם ארץ. חשך מלשון ערבי
sources.says: Radak says it means darkened, from Arabic.

sources.quote: נעתם, בלשון קדר כמו חשך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says in the language of Kedar it means darkened.

9:19.headline: Right and left mean south and north
9:19.body: ימין is the right hand, but facing east it is also the south. The Targum reads 'south' and 'north' here. The Talmud learns from this verse that the south wind has brought no rain since the Temple fell.

sources.quote: וּבַז מִן דָרוֹמָא
sources.says: The Targum renders 'on the right' as 'from the south'.

sources.quote: מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא הוּגְשְׁמָה רוּחַ דְּרוֹמִית
sources.says: The Talmud says that since the Temple was destroyed the south wind has not brought rain, citing this verse.

9:19.headline: "His arm" or "his seed": the same letters
9:19.body: זרעו can be read זְרֹעוֹ 'his arm' or זַרְעוֹ 'his offspring'. The Talmud says: do not read 'the flesh of his arm' but 'the flesh of his seed'. Another passage takes 'arm' literally, of a famine.

sources.quote: אַל תִּקְרֵי ״בְּשַׂר זְרוֹעוֹ״ אֶלָּא ״בְּשַׂר זַרְעוֹ״
sources.says: The Talmud says not to read 'the flesh of his arm' but 'the flesh of his seed'.

sources.quote: שְׁבִיעִית בְּשַׂר זְרוֹעוֹתֵיהֶם
sources.says: The Talmud says that in the seventh year of a famine they ate the flesh of their own arms.

sources.quote: גְבַר נִכְסֵיהּ קָרִיבֵיהּ יִבְזוּן
sources.says: The Targum reads it as each man plundering the goods of his relative.
